new.title: Cancel end / cancel shut-out skips the order's approval gate when sent through collectiveOrder.transition
new.body: Step 15 (and the step 27 close): the order flow's end_order and shut_out gates are meant to stop anyone rewinding an order's process state until the order's review has passed. The bulk path collectiveOrder.batch enforces this. It gates cancel_end on end_order and cancel_shut_out on shut_out for every id. The single-order collectiveOrder.transition endpoint, which accepts process: "not_shut_out", gates only the forward moves (process === "finished" and process === "shut_out"). It does not gate a move back to not_shut_out. PROCESS_TRANSITIONS allows finished -> not_shut_out and shut_out -> not_shut_out, so any holder of collectiveOrder.lifecycle.process (ops, branch-manager, admin) can reopen a finished or shut-out order on an org with the gates ticked, without the approval the batch path demands. The web UI routes row actions through batch, so this is reachable through the API only. It is still the same state change with a different guard.
new.note: found by zyt-audit (unenforced-approval)

new.title: An approved order can be deleted outright: the approval freezes its edits but not its existence
new.body: Step 15: once accounting approves an order, collectiveOrder.update (and updateBatch) refuse further edits through assertPostApprovalEditable, so the approved content is frozen. collectiveOrder.delete checks only under-review and locked, and the batch delete action checks only assertNoneUnderReview. So an approved, unlocked order, together with its unbilled cost lines (removed by clearOrderCostLines), can be deleted by any collectiveOrder.delete holder. Nobody re-reviews it and the approver is not told. This is the same asymmetry as the fee item s21-an-approved-fee-can-be-deleted-outright-approval, here on the order record.
new.note: found by zyt-audit (unenforced-approval)

new.title: An approved bill of lading can be deleted, though even its attachments are frozen after approval
new.body: Steps 16 and 18: after the director approves a B/L, lading.update and lading.deleteAttachment both call assertPostApprovalEditable, so the approved B/L and even its attached files cannot be changed. lading.delete and lading.bulkDelete call only assertNotUnderReview. Any lading.delete holder can therefore delete an approved B/L outright, one at a time or in bulk, with no re-review. The approval binds the B/L's fields and attachments but not the record itself.

new.title: Post to cost ledger is offered to Sales, but only roles holding expense.costLine.import can run it
new.body: At step 11 the SOP gives the quotation to Sales, and the editor menu offers 'Post to cost ledger' on any approved quotation that is won or converted. The check looks only at audit and outcome status, never at a permission. The server gates importFromQuote on expense.costLine.import. Sales hold only expense.costLine.read, so every salesperson who presses it gets FORBIDDEN. The node is held by admin, branch-manager, ops (expense.costLine subtree) and accounting.

new.title: Expense entry lets Sales and Accounting fill fee rows and press Save, then the server refuses the save
new.body: Step 20 says that collectiveOrder:read to open the order and collectiveOrder.update to save are enough. The Expense entry grid and its Save button are disabled only when the order is locked, never on a permission. On the server, saveChildren also needs expense.costLine.create for any new row, expense.costLine.update for any changed row and expense.costLine.delete for removed rows. (1) Sales hold collectiveOrder.update but only expense.costLine.read. A salesperson who goes to Expense entry straight after converting (steps 11-12) can add rows with 'Costs name' and press Save, and gets 'Missing permission: expense.costLine.create'. (2) Accounting is granted collectiveOrder.detail because fees are the half of the order accounting owns, but it does not hold collectiveOrder.update. The grid is fully editable for them, yet every save fails at the procedure guard.

new.title: An approval tells nobody: My tasks carries rejections back but never approvals forward
new.body: Steps 8 to 9 and 15 to 16: when a reviewer approves a quotation or an order, the submission becomes passed and only the audit log and the status cache change. My tasks has four row kinds: decide, resubmit (rejected submissions only), unstick and reply. No kind picks up a passed submission. A salesperson whose quotation was approved gets no 'approved, send it now' task. Documentation gets no queue of approved orders still waiting for a bill of lading. A search of api and web found no 'approved order without a B/L' query; the only lading count is on the order's own record page. Each next person has to poll the ledgers to find out that their step is unblocked.

new.title: Bill review hides withdrawal requests that are waiting for the reviewer's consent
new.body: Step 23: the seeded Bill review flow is the only seeded flow with withdrawal mode requires_reviewer_approval. When an accountant retracts a bill after any stage has passed, the submission moves to withdrawal_under_review. Its audit-status cache then reads withdraw_pending, and only the routed accounting or director reviewer can approve the retraction. /approve/bill mounts BillsPage in review mode, and that page seeds its filter to auditStatus = pending. bills.list applies that as an exact match on the cache column, on top of awaitingMyReview. So the row the engine routed to this reviewer is filtered out of the queue they open, including when they arrive from My tasks → Decide, which links to plain /approve/bill. The Quotation, Cost, Shipment and Expense-template queues dropped this same seed under NCTAI-266 because it emptied the withdrawal reviewer's queue. Bill review, the one queue whose seeded flow actually produces withdrawal reviews, still has the seed. The page only hints at this in its empty state, so when other pending bills are listed the withdrawal is hidden with no hint. The presets do not help either: 'My withdrawals' filters on submittedBy = me, which is the submitter's view, not the reviewer's. Until a reviewer clears the filter by hand, the bill stays under review and frozen (no invoice, no write-off, no edit), and the submitter cannot finish the correction.

new.title: The profit statement and profit trend count a foreign-currency bill that has no exchange rate as if its rate were 1
new.body: costLines.createBill can create a bill in a foreign currency while the rate is missing. It returns a rateMissing banner and leaves bill.exchange_rate NULL. Later, at month-end (step 27), getProfitStatement and getProfitAnalysis convert each bill into local currency with coalesce(bill.exchangeRate, 1). A USD 1,000 bill with no rate therefore lands in the local-currency receivable, payable, gross profit and actual profit as 1,000 local. getFinancialSummary returns a missingRate / billsMissingRate count beside its roll-up so the UI can mark it incomplete. These two endpoints return no such count. Their summary totals look complete when they are wrong, and the accountant or director reading the profit figures has no sign that some bills were never converted. The byCurrency breakdown is the only unconverted view.
